history.caption: A perfect supply plan still fails if it begins with a false count.
history.title: Stock Record Balance Mismatch

style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio product photograph, 100mm macro lens with a razor-sharp focal plane and shallow depth of field. An asymmetric composition off-centre to the right showing a precision industrial mechanical balance scale made of brushed steel and frosted copper. One side of the balance holds a heavy, textured matte polymer cargo module, while the other side holds an empty, mismatched weight tray, visibly out of equilibrium. Softbox key light with visible falloff casting a long, deep shadow across a textured dark basalt surface. Minimalist, premium editorial standard, quiet confidence, sophisticated muted teal and amber color palette.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, typography, UI elements, watermarks, text
rationale: The story revolves around a fundamental mismatch in accounting or measurement (the record vs the physical count). A studio product shot of a precision balancing mechanism beautifully captures this core tension of measurement and mismatch, providing a clean, striking visual.
cue: The stock record the plan reads is wrong
subject: a precision industrial balance scale showing a mismatch
core_thesis: Stock records are frequently wrong at the product group level, meaning supply plans begin with a false count that cuts profit.
core_conflict: Physical stock reality vs ERP software record claims
composition: asymmetric composition off-centre to the right, generous negative space on the left
alt_text: False Stock Records. A precision industrial balance scale out of equilibrium, with a heavy polymer module on one side and an empty tray on the other.
caption: False Stock Records: How false shelf counts ruin perfect supply forecasts.
title: False Stock Records
